title: Transit union agreement and carried-over by-laws
subtitle: Short special meeting: closed session on labour relations, three by-laws approved, and a conflict declaration.
overview: Council held a short special meeting before the evening's delegation session. It met in closed session on labour relations and then reported back publicly that staff were directed to finalize and execute a Memorandum of Agreement with the Amalgamated Transit Union Local 1189, which represents Guelph transit operators and staff. This was announced after the closed session and was not decided by a separate open motion.

Council then approved three by-laws carried over from the November 13 meeting. By-laws 21008 and 21009 were approved {{vote:m2}}, with one councillor stepping out because the properties involved are owned by that councillor's employer. By-law 21013 was approved {{vote:m3}}.

For residents, the agreement is meant to provide stability for the people who operate local transit. The by-law approvals complete items left over from the earlier meeting. Council then adjourned {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved these two by-laws carried over from November 13, with Councillor Caron not voting after declaring a conflict of interest {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved the third carried-over by-law {{vote:m3}}.

debate: There was no substantive debate on the by-laws; the mayor asked if there was anything further on each and none was raised.
A councillor asked that by-laws 21008 and 21009 be voted on separately, saying a conflict had been declared earlier at the planning meeting because the properties relate to the councillor's employer.
In the statement after closed session, the mayor thanked the city and union bargaining teams and said transit operators and staff provide valued service to the community.
